why: Customers describe a smaller fix found first
Your About page returns a “page missing” message, so a visitor can't find out who you are.

Your customers already describe the plumber you are. Vanessa F.: “Another company told me I had to pay thousand of dollars to fix the sewer line… Brandon to the rescue.” Today those words sit on Google, not on your site.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already describe the company you are. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we’ll walk you through this demo and what a full build adds.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your site says you serve Wichita and a 30 mile radius around Sedgwick County, your Google listing puts you at 836 S Broadview St in Wichita, and a Birdeye listing and one Google review say Cheney, so which address should every listing use?
Your page titles say Plumb Crazy, LLC while your footer says Plumb Crazy Kansas, LLC, so which name should every listing use?
Your drain cleaning page says 17 years of experience and your sewer cleaning page says over 16 years, with no founding year anywhere, so which number should every listing use?
Your reviews describe a smaller fix found before a big quote, and this demo leads with that, so is that how your team works, and how would you put it?

lead.heading: Why we led with the smaller fix first
lead.text: The scariest moment for a Wichita homeowner is being handed a big quote and told it has to be done. We led with the smaller fix because it rests on things Google can't find anywhere else: your customers' own accounts, your seven days a week with no emergency rates, and the Wichita-area details on your pages. That is also why it can help you rank, and please tell us if it isn't how you work.
